title: A connection pool
hints: Keep two `#` arrays: the free resources and the checked-out ones. `available` is a getter over the free one. For the error class, call `super(message)` first, then set `this.name` and `this.capacity`.

`acquire` takes from the front of the free list (`shift()`) and records the resource as checked out. `release` finds it in the checked-out list with `indexOf`; `-1` means throw, otherwise `splice` it out and `push` it onto the back of the free list. `use` is acquire, then `try { return fn(r); } finally { this.release(r); }`.

acquire(): T { if (this.#free.length === 0) throw new PoolExhaustedError(this.#capacity); const r = this.#free.shift() as T; this.#inUse.push(r); return r; } — set `#capacity` in the constructor from `resources.length`, and copy the array with `[...resources]` so you don't modify the caller's list.
